newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares gain on political news.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares gain on political news.

text.p: Delhi shares traded higher at mid-session on Friday following sizeable buying by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and speculators on expectations that a political crisis might end soon, brokers said.
They said prices also moved up due to stronger than usual demand in Delhi because most of the other major stock exchanges of the country were closed for the Moslem festival Id al-Adha.
At 12:45 p.m. (0715 GMT), the benchmark index had risen 6.40 points to 776.28.
"Despite a rally in stock prices, the definite trend of the market would depend on political developments," said Sanjay Mittal of brokers S.R.M. Securities.

The Congress party on Friday wrote to President Shankar Dayal Sharma offering to renew vital support to the United Front coalition and abandon its own claim to power if the alliance chose a new leader to replace caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
The coalition prepared to pick a new leader to succeed Deve Gowda, who lost a confidence vote on April 11 by a huge margin resulting from the withdrawal of Congress support on March 30.
Reliance Industies shot up 4.50 rupees to 286.40 and TISCO rose 5.50 rupees to 175.00 on buying by foreign and domestic financial institutions, brokers said.
State Bank of India quoted 7.05 rupees higher at 304.30.
